summary: A [National Strategy for Digital Governance](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Governance in São Tomé and Príncipe) adopted in 2020 runs on nine thematic axes, and a [Public Administration Reform Strategy](2025-06-18-ministra-justica-digitalizacao-setor-publico) approved in 2025 names electronic governance its essential pillar.
developments:
The digital governance strategy is a whole-of-government instrument on nine axes; the source page is undated and the year is taken from its context, so even the strategy's own date rests on inference ([strategy](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Governance in São Tomé and Príncipe)).

The reform strategy was presented as newly approved in June 2025 with electronic governance named as its essential pillar ([reform](2025-06-18-ministra-justica-digitalizacao-setor-publico)).

Neither carries a target, budget, milestone or review published anywhere the base can reach, so what either instrument commits the state to is unstated.

summary: A [revision of the regulatory framework](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) covering the regulatory entities law and the electronic communications law was approved by the Council of Ministers and sent to the National Assembly.
developments:
The regulator's own statute was already approved, and the two laws went to the Assembly in 2025; no later source confirms parliamentary passage ([revision](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

The 2020 digital governance strategy remains the framing instrument, on nine thematic axes ([strategy](2024-01-01 National Strategy for Digital Governance in São Tomé and Príncipe)), and a published national data strategy joined it in July 2025 ([data strategy](2025-07-01-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-politica-governanca-de-dados)).

What is missing is the sector instrument between them: no ICT or broadband plan with targets, costings or a delivery timetable is held, and the two bills have sat with the legislature for a year with nothing published about their progress.

summary: No broadband strategy is held; the only dated instrument in the window is the regulator's [provisional authorisation of an IPTV service](2026-01-01-ager-autoriza-provisoriamente-cst-iptv-plataforma-cst-on) over the incumbent's platform.
developments:
The regulator approved a resolution provisionally authorising the incumbent to carry IPTV over its own platform, stating the aim as developing and diversifying electronic communications services ([authorisation](2026-01-01-ager-autoriza-provisoriamente-cst-iptv-plataforma-cst-on)).

That is a service authorisation, not a plan for broadband coverage, targets or funding. No broadband strategy, national broadband plan or coverage target is published anywhere the base reaches, and the universal service instrument that would carry one dates from 2012 ([universal service](2012-08-20-sao-tome-decreto-lei-19-2012-servico-universal-telecomunicacoes)).

summary: A [national interoperability framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01) has stood at draft version 0.1 since November 2021, with mandatory and recommended technical specifications and no later version held.
developments:
Version 0.1 was developed by two United Nations bodies in consultation with the identity institute and published on its portal, setting out scope, per-dimension policies, a compliance regime and technical specifications ([framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01)).

A sectoral interoperability platform was delivered in the window: the electoral reform project presented a platform linking the civil registry databases to the electoral roll, built by a Portuguese university ([platform](2025-09-01-prese-nota-imprensa-recenseamento-eleitoral-automatico-interoperabilidade)).

So the framework a whole-of-government exchange would be built to remains a draft five years old, while the one working linkage was built to a project's own design.

summary: There is [no national AI strategy](2025-01-01-unesco-sao-tome-ai-readiness-assessment-full-report); the readiness assessment puts approval of an AI law at 2027 or 2028 and rates it low priority against four legal updates it rates high.
developments:
The assessment's roadmap puts approval of a National AI Strategy Law at 2027 or 2028 at low priority, arguing the instrument must be a law because personal-rights matters are reserved to the National Assembly, and rates four updates high priority for 2024 or 2025 instead: the data protection agency's 2017 organic law, the 2008 decree creating the innovation institute, the 2020 resolution adopting the digital governance strategy, and the statistics institute's capacity ([roadmap](2025-01-01-unesco-sao-tome-ai-readiness-assessment-full-report)).

The education minister's preface states the country is not prepared to implement artificial intelligence ethically, having neither a strategy nor an AI-specific law nor a national AI ethics commission ([preface](2025-01-01-unesco-sao-tome-ai-readiness-assessment-full-report)); a later country profile drawn from the same assessment restates the absence ([profile](2026-01-22-unesco-sao-tome-ai-ethics-governance-country-profile)).

What has happened instead is training: a two-day intensive on digitalisation and artificial intelligence for the public administration ran in April 2026, financed by a bilateral agency ([training](2026-04-22-rstp-pnud-capacitacao-digitalizacao-inteligencia-artificial)). Preparation is under way and the instrument is not.

summary: The identity institute states that hosting the country's vital systems [in national territory is an imperative of security and sovereignty](2026-01-01-inic-sao-tome-alojamento-web-soberania-territorio-nacional), and offers the hosting service itself.
developments:
The institute's own service page states the sovereignty position and adds that the personal data protection law restricts hosting personal information outside the country; it offers hosting to the whole public administration and invites private bodies to use it ([hosting](2026-01-01-inic-sao-tome-alojamento-web-soberania-territorio-nacional)).

That is a stated position and a service, not a binding localisation rule: the page is undated, no instrument setting a residency requirement is held, and the restriction it cites is a transfer condition in the data protection law rather than a localisation mandate.

The data protection authority named international data transfer among the priority themes of a new Lusophone regulators' network in August 2025, which is cooperation rather than a national rule ([network](2025-09-02-anpdp-primeiro-encontro-rede-lusofona-protecao-dados)).

summary: The identity institute published [version 1 of a national data strategy and roadmap](2025-07-01-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-politica-governanca-de-dados) in July 2025, and a [capacity building workshop](2026-07-13 D4D Hub on Sao Tome and Principe) on adopting the continental framework followed in July 2026.
developments:
The strategy sets objectives for responsible and ethical data use, data-based decision-making and an innovation-oriented culture, and treats artificial intelligence as an opportunity to be explored using public data rather than as anything in operation ([strategy](2025-07-01-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-politica-governanca-de-dados)).

The workshop ran over two days with a European development hub, a continental development agency and a regional civil-society network ([workshop](2026-07-13 D4D Hub on Sao Tome and Principe)).

A lender mission had reported the data strategy as remaining in draft ([mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)); a published version 1 is the movement. No adoption instrument, budget or implementation report follows either document.

summary: The [2016 personal data protection law](2016-05-10-sao-tome-lei-03-2016-proteccao-dados-pessoais) is in force and establishes the national authority; it is modelled on a European directive Europe itself replaced in 2018.
developments:
The gazette text is now held: the law guarantees and protects the personal data of natural persons and establishes the national personal data protection agency as supervisory authority ([law](2016-05-10-sao-tome-lei-03-2016-proteccao-dados-pessoais)). The capture is truncated inside Artigo 45, so the later articles are not readable here.

A secondary legal survey records the modelling on the superseded European directive and the penalties, and remains the only source describing the regime's operation ([survey](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

Modelling on a directive replaced in 2018 is the substantive point: the regime the authority enforces is a generation behind the standard its cooperation partners work to.

The country is a signatory to the continental cyber and data convention, with ratification status not stated ([convention](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

summary: A [2017 cybercrime statute](2017-10-06-sao-tome-lei-15-2017-lei-sobre-cibercrime) creates the computer-crime offences, sets the procedural powers for electronic evidence and requires a 24-hour police contact point.
developments:
Artigo 1 states that the law establishes substantive and procedural criminal provisions and provisions on international cooperation relating to cybercrime and the collection of electronic evidence, adapting domestic law to the international conventions ([statute](2017-10-06-sao-tome-lei-15-2017-lei-sobre-cibercrime)).

It creates offences of computer forgery, damage to programs or data, computer sabotage, illegal access, illegal interception and illegitimate reproduction of a protected program, and requires the judicial police to keep a permanent international cooperation contact point ([statute](2017-10-06-sao-tome-lei-15-2017-lei-sobre-cibercrime)).

A national cybersecurity strategy for 2024 to 2028 exists in draft and went to public consultation in September 2025 ([consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca)); the statute is in force and the strategy is not.

summary: An [aggregated identification document law](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) was flagged as urgent by a lender mission in 2025, its absence stated as a potential constraint on data collection, and no later source confirms passage.
developments:
The mission flagged review, public consultation, finalisation and approval as urgent ([law](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

A year later nothing records movement. The foundational digital identity it would govern has live prototypes and a system integrator engaged, so the build is running ahead of the statute — the same order this frame finds in most units.

summary: The [2018 payment system law](2018-09-07-sao-tome-lei-17-2018-sistema-nacional-de-pagamentos) is in force, a [new central bank organic law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp) replaced the 1992 statute in 2025, and the [2026 budget law caps cash payments](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado) at 10,000 dobras.
developments:
The payment system law applies to payment systems and providers operating in the country, makes the central bank regulator and overseer, and carries a chapter on electronic funds transfers between individuals, commercial entities and financial institutions ([law](2018-09-07-sao-tome-lei-17-2018-sistema-nacional-de-pagamentos)).

The 2025 organic law sets the bank's attributions to regulate and oversee payment systems and to license and supervise financial institutions ([organic law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp)).

Article 9 of the 2026 budget law prohibits taxpayers with organised accounting from making or receiving cash payments of 10,000 dobras or more and requires a means identifying the payee, with cash spending above the limit not tax-deductible ([budget law](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado)). That is the first instrument in this base compelling electronic settlement rather than enabling it.

summary: A [National Framework for Interoperability](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data)) was enacted as Law 1/2024 for public-sector data sharing, and only a secondary legal survey describes it.
developments:
The law is held through the same 2024 legal-survey chapter as the data-protection law, not through its own text ([law](2024-01-01 São Tomé and Príncipe - Digital Regulations in the Metaverse Era (Data))).

It is the stated legal basis for the civil-registry to electoral-database linkage recorded separately, and the base now also holds a civil-registry exchange interface ([interface](2023-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-legi-non-troca-dados-registos)), a health platform ([health](2020-01-01-sao-tome-ministerio-saude-sistema-informacao-saude-dhis2)) and a social protection system integrated with the social registry ([social protection](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon)).

Each was built to its own design. The framework the law would be applied through is a draft from 2021 ([framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01)), so the statute has evidenced uses and no published specification behind them.

summary: There are [no AI-specific laws or regulations](2026-01-22-unesco-sao-tome-ai-ethics-governance-country-profile) and no national AI ethics commission; the data protection law and its authority are the only governance anchors.
developments:
The readiness assessment finds no specific legal provision on artificial intelligence and names the 2016 personal data protection law and the 2017 cybercrime law as the nearest anchors, the cybercrime law needing updating to cover artificial intelligence; there is consequently no national AI ethics commission or dedicated governance structure ([assessment](2025-01-01-unesco-sao-tome-ai-readiness-assessment-full-report)).

The same assessment records that the data protection law makes it an administrative offence, punishable by fine, for a body notified by the authority to keep open network access available to controllers not complying with the law ([assessment](2025-01-01-unesco-sao-tome-ai-readiness-assessment-full-report)); the innovation institute can issue strategies and guidelines but these do not carry the force of law ([profile](2026-01-22-unesco-sao-tome-ai-ethics-governance-country-profile)).

An AI justice platform is meanwhile being built with a chatbot trained on national legislation ([platform](2026-06-01-sao-tome-unodc-direitosaopovo-ai-justice-platform)): the first public-facing AI system arrives ahead of any rule governing one.

summary: The [1998 statistics law](1998-08-31-sao-tome-lei-5-98-bases-do-sistema-estatistico-nacional) defines the national statistical system, creates the statistics institute and sets a regime of statistical secrecy and transgressions.
developments:
The law names the national statistics council, the statistics institute, the central bank and the institute's delegated organs as the system's organs, creates the institute in Artigo 7 as the body producing and analysing official statistics, and sets fines in Artigos 11 to 15 ([law](1998-08-31-sao-tome-lei-5-98-bases-do-sistema-estatistico-nacional)).

It was passed by the National Assembly on 12 August 1998 and promulgated on 31 August 1998 ([law](1998-08-31-sao-tome-lei-5-98-bases-do-sistema-estatistico-nacional)). Nothing amending or replacing it is held, so a statistical system now running a census, a household budget survey and an automatic electoral register rests on an instrument written before any of them.

summary: There is no access-to-information statute; the [constitution's three relevant articles](2003-01-01-sao-tome-constituicao-republica-democratica) are the whole of the national guarantee.
developments:
Artigo 29 gives everyone the right freely to express and disseminate thought by word, image or any other means; Artigo 74 places on holders of political office the duty to keep citizens informed about public affairs; Artigo 76 provides that absence of publication renders laws legally ineffective ([constitution](2003-01-01-sao-tome-constituicao-republica-democratica)).

None of the three creates a request procedure, a deadline, an exemption regime, an appeal or an oversight body ([constitution](2003-01-01-sao-tome-constituicao-republica-democratica)). Without those, a right to information is a principle rather than a route a citizen can take, and no route is held.

summary: The authority was [assigned to supervise the civil-registry to electoral-database interconnection](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp), and [signed a cooperation memorandum with a Macau counterpart](2026-06-10-dspdp-macau-formaliza-cooperacao-protecao-dados-stp) covering cross-border flows and artificial-intelligence supervision.
developments:
Supervision of the interconnection was assigned in April 2026, which is the only instance in this base of a data-protection authority being given oversight of a specific interoperability project at the point it goes live ([supervision](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp)).

The memorandum was signed in June 2026 covering cross-border data flows, artificial-intelligence supervision, awareness, training and joint studies ([memorandum](2026-06-10-dspdp-macau-formaliza-cooperacao-protecao-dados-stp), [pacts](2026-05-27-macau-to-sign-data-protection-pacts-stp-cabo-verde)).

The authority is also a founding member of a recently created Lusophone data-protection network, hosted for a cooperation visit by the Portuguese commission ([network](2025-06-23-cnpd-portugal-recebeu-anpdp-stp-rede-lusofona)). Its supervisory output — findings, penalties, registrations — is not published at any date.

summary: The [2016 law](2016-05-10-sao-tome-lei-03-2016-proteccao-dados-pessoais) creates the supervisory authority, which has since taken [supervision of a live interoperability project](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp) and joined two international networks.
developments:
The statutory basis is now held in its own gazette text rather than through a secondary survey ([law](2016-05-10-sao-tome-lei-03-2016-proteccao-dados-pessoais)).

The authority was assigned to supervise the civil-registry to electoral-database interconnection in April 2026 ([supervision](2026-04-15-recenseamento-automatico-fiscalizado-anpdp)), is a founding member of a Lusophone data-protection network ([network](2025-06-23-cnpd-portugal-recebeu-anpdp-stp-rede-lusofona)), and signed a cooperation memorandum with a Macau counterpart in June 2026 ([memorandum](2026-06-10-dspdp-macau-formaliza-cooperacao-protecao-dados-stp)).

Readiness in the sense the indicator asks about is thinner than the activity: no register of controllers, no published finding, no penalty and no annual report appears at any date.

summary: The country is one of seven covered by a [programme for African developing island economies](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch), and takes part in a [Lusophone data governance workshop series](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa) and [regional digital governance dialogues](2026-03-31-palop-digital-identity-collaboration-biometricupdate).
developments:
The island economies programme was launched at a ministerial segment in July 2026; it is a seven-state programme and no national commitments beyond the communique are detailed ([programme](2026-07-24-auda-nepad-island-economies-programme-launch)).

A second Lusophone data governance workshop was held in June 2026, and the country's specific national content from it is not detailed ([workshop](2026-07-28-advancing-data-infrastructure-and-governance-in-lusophone-africa)).

A second webinar in the regional digital governance series covered digital identity as foundational infrastructure, again from a multi-country source with no national content separated out ([dialogues](2026-03-31-palop-digital-identity-collaboration-biometricupdate)). Three regional forums, and in none of them can the base say what this country said or undertook.

summary: The country hosted a [regional regulators' workshop on universal connectivity](2025-11-01-ager-sao-tome-workshop-arctel-uit-conectividade-universal) in November 2025, closing on a joint commitment to continued regulatory harmonisation.
developments:
The workshop was organised by the international telecommunications body with the national regulator and the Lusophone regulators' association, bringing together regulators from the member states, specialists and national technicians on promoting and measuring universal and meaningful connectivity ([workshop](2025-11-01-ager-sao-tome-workshop-arctel-uit-conectividade-universal)).

The regulator's technical administrator described it as a step towards keeping the country aligned with international best practice, and the meeting closed on a joint commitment to continue technical cooperation and regulatory harmonisation among Portuguese-speaking countries ([workshop](2025-11-01-ager-sao-tome-workshop-arctel-uit-conectividade-universal)).

No harmonised instrument, model law or transposition follows it in anything held. The page carries no date and the month is inferred.

progress: Mixed, the regional cable was financed and built a decade ago while the inter-island cable it should feed has slipped on procurement
summary: The country's stake in the [regional submarine cable](2015-06-17-world-bank-icr-central-african-backbone-apl2-sao-tome) was financed and built through a shared vehicle in 2015; the [inter-island cable](2025-10-20-world-bank-isr-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-seq7) has since cut its project rating on procurement delays.
developments:
A grant of US$14.9 million equivalent financed the country's contribution to the regional optical fibre cable on an open-access basis, structured through a special purpose vehicle into which government and operator contributions were made as a long-term shareholder loan ([completion report](2015-06-17-world-bank-icr-central-african-backbone-apl2-sao-tome)).

The national instrument behind it put a second telecommunications licence and the state's holding in the vehicle to public tender together ([tender decree](2012-11-12-sao-tome-decreto-38-2012-concurso-segunda-licenca-stp-cabo-ace)).

In October 2025 the lender cut its rating for the digital project's development objective from satisfactory to moderately satisfactory on ongoing challenges with procurement of the cable to the second island, while most other activities progressed ([status report](2025-10-20-world-bank-isr-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-seq7)). The regional cable is in service and the domestic leg to the smaller island is not.

summary: The [national interoperability framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01) sets mandatory and recommended technical standards across its component segments, and has stood at draft version 0.1 since 2021.
developments:
The framework sets out definitions, purpose and scope, general and per-dimension policies, the compliance regime, governance and revision arrangements, and technical specifications for its components ([framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01)).

It is version 0.1 of November 2021 and no successor version, approval instrument or compliance report is held ([framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01)). A compliance regime in a draft nobody has adopted binds nothing, and the systems built since have each set their own interfaces.

summary: The [national quality body](2026-01-01-senapiq-stp-servico-nacional-propriedade-intelectual-e-qualidade) is an autonomous public institute under the finance ministry covering industrial property, standardisation, certification and accreditation.
developments:
The body states that it has administrative, financial, technical and asset autonomy under the ministry responsible for industry, and that its functions include proposing policies on industrial property, copyright and related rights, standardisation, certification and accreditation ([body](2026-01-01-senapiq-stp-servico-nacional-propriedade-intelectual-e-qualidade)).

No national standards catalogue, accreditation register or published certification scheme is held, so what the mandate has produced cannot be read here. The page carries no date and the year is inferred.

summary: The country is a [correspondent member of the international standards organisation](2026-01-01-iso-senapiq-stp-correspondent-member-sao-tome), and the [first bank certified to a quality management standard](2026-08-03-telanon-bgfi-bank-sao-tome-primeiro-banco-certificado-iso-9001) was recognised in August 2026.
developments:
The membership record gives the category as correspondent member and names the national quality body as the member institution ([membership](2026-01-01-iso-senapiq-stp-correspondent-member-sao-tome)). Correspondent membership is the category for countries without a fully developed national standards activity, which is the position it records.

A bank became the first in the country to obtain the quality management certification, presented at a ceremony marking 55 years of its group and attended by members of the government, the central bank and the diplomatic corps ([certification](2026-08-03-telanon-bgfi-bank-sao-tome-primeiro-banco-certificado-iso-9001)).

A single private certification is the whole of the in-window adoption record; no public body is recorded as certified to any international standard.

summary: A [first internet governance forum](2026-07-31-ager-1a-edicao-fgi-stp-sao-tome) was held over three days in July 2026, opened by the prime minister.
developments:
The first edition was convened by the regulator and opened by the head of government ([forum](2026-07-31-ager-1a-edicao-fgi-stp-sao-tome)).

No outcome document, participant count or commitment is published, and it is a first edition, so nothing yet establishes whether it becomes a standing channel.

The one other route the base holds is also the regulator's: two public consultations on draft regulatory instruments ([consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca)). Both channels sit with the regulator rather than with a ministry or the legislature.

summary: The regulator ran a [second public consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca) in September 2025, on the draft national cybersecurity strategy, having [published its own responses](2024-01-01-ager-sao-tome-relatorio-consulta-publica-lei-comunicacoes-electronicas) to the first.
developments:
The first consultation, on the draft electronic communications law, was launched in February 2024 and the regulator published a report setting out its legal basis and its point-by-point responses to the contributions received ([report](2024-01-01-ager-sao-tome-relatorio-consulta-publica-lei-comunicacoes-electronicas)).

The second put the 2024 to 2028 national cybersecurity strategy and its annexed action plan to public comment under the digital project, with contributions due within 30 days of publication and later submissions excluded ([consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca)).

Both are the regulator's, on regulatory instruments. No consultation by a ministry, and no record of what either consultation changed, is held.

summary: The state budget is published each year, most recently as [Lei n. 3/2026](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado), and no digital-transformation appropriation line is identified in anything the base holds.
developments:
The 2025 budget document, published by the finance ministry's budget directorate, covers the year's budget, technical explanations and the balance of 2024 execution ([budget](2025-02-01-sao-tome-ministerio-economia-financas-orcamento-geral-do-estado-2025)), and the 2026 budget was enacted as a law gazetted in March 2026 ([law](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado)).

A civil-society citizen's budget for 2026 summarises how the State plans to raise and spend public resources and links to the official text ([citizen's budget](2025-12-01-cipstp-orcamento-do-cidadao-stp-2026)).

None of the three identifies an appropriation for digital transformation. Every system recorded in this unit is donor-financed, and the budget documents held do not show the domestic side of that ledger at all.

summary: The bilateral relationship with China was [elevated to a strategic partnership](2024-09-05-china-mfa-xi-jinping-meets-prime-minister-sao-tome-strategic-partnership) in September 2024, announced by the two heads of government in Beijing.
developments:
The Chinese foreign ministry, as one of the two parties, records that the prime minister met the president in Beijing during a summit and an official visit on 5 September 2024, and that the two leaders announced the elevation of the relationship to a strategic partnership ([communique](2024-09-05-china-mfa-xi-jinping-meets-prime-minister-sao-tome-strategic-partnership)).

No financial terms, sums or sectoral annexes are stated in the signing party's own release, and no implementing instrument has followed it into the base.

The one other strategic-scale instrument recorded for this country is a citizenship-fund contract stated only by a consulate ([contract](2025-10-13-sao-tome-consulate-berlin-atlas-sovereign-iopn-ai-investment)). Both are announcements of intent whose content the base cannot read.

summary: The one instrument on record bringing non-state capital into infrastructure is the [2012 tender](2012-11-12-sao-tome-decreto-38-2012-concurso-segunda-licenca-stp-cabo-ace) of a second telecommunications licence and the state's cable holding, settled through a [shared vehicle](2015-06-17-world-bank-icr-central-african-backbone-apl2-sao-tome).
developments:
The tender's stated object was both the award of a second licence to establish and operate a public telecommunications network and the cession, in whole or in part, of the State's holding in the cable company together with the corresponding capacity in the submarine cable ([decree](2012-11-12-sao-tome-decreto-38-2012-concurso-segunda-licenca-stp-cabo-ace)).

The completion report records that government and operator contributions were made into the vehicle as a long-term shareholder loan, enabling national access to cable capacity ([report](2015-06-17-world-bank-icr-central-african-backbone-apl2-sao-tome)).

Nothing since brings private capital into a digital asset on this record. The citizenship-fund contract reported in October 2025 names a ten-billion-dollar ambition and no counterparty document was located ([contract](2025-10-13-sao-tome-consulate-berlin-atlas-sovereign-iopn-ai-investment)).

summary: A [lender digital project](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) had disbursed 36 per cent by September 2025, and the window added an [energy grant of US$24.5 million](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant) and [US$6 million more for social protection](2025-10-14-sao-tome-world-bank-social-protection-additional-financing).
developments:
The digital project finances the digital identity, the citizen portal, the interoperability platform, the incident response team and the data-centre work ([project](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025), [approval](2022-06-15-wb-stp-001-digital-sao-tome-and-principe)), and its rating for the development objective was cut to moderately satisfactory in October 2025 on cable procurement ([status report](2025-10-20-world-bank-isr-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-seq7)).

An African development fund grant of US$24.5 million was approved in April 2026, anchoring a US$30 million energy transition project ([grant](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant)), and US$6 million in additional financing was signed for the cash transfer project in October 2025 ([financing](2025-10-14-sao-tome-world-bank-social-protection-additional-financing)). A US$10 million policy operation followed in March 2026 covering fiscal, energy and digital connectivity ([operation](2026-03-11-world-bank-sao-tome-dpf-fiscal-energy-digital-connectivity)).

A payment system and financial inclusion grant of about US$3.34m has been active since 2017 ([grant](2017-01-01-afdb-stp-001-sao-tome-and-principe---payments)).

summary: The incumbent operator [inaugurated its 35th antenna](2026-03-27-cst-inaugura-antena-agua-ize) in March 2026, on a network expansion running alongside a school connectivity plan.
developments:
The 35th antenna was inaugurated in a coastal district in March 2026 ([antenna](2026-03-27-cst-inaugura-antena-agua-ize), [expansion](2025-01-25-cst-35-anos-expansao-rede-conectividade-escolas)).

No coverage percentage, subscriber count or population-served figure accompanies it, so the antenna count is the only measure of the network the base holds. For a two-island state, a count of masts is a more meaningful measure than it would be elsewhere, and it is still not coverage.

summary: Broadband use is now carried in a [financing operation's results framework at 146,000 people](2026-03-11-world-bank-sao-tome-dpf-fiscal-energy-digital-connectivity) at December 2025, against [regulator figures](2024-11-01-sao-tome-ager-observatorio-estatistico-2023) of 2.6 fixed and 43.3 mobile broadband per 100 inhabitants in 2023.
developments:
The regulator's sector statistics for 2023 report 5,775 fixed broadband subscribers at a penetration rate of 2.6 per 100 inhabitants and 96,901 active mobile broadband accesses at 43.3 per 100, with installed international capacity of 35,840 Gb against 6,122 Gb used ([statistics](2024-11-01-sao-tome-ager-observatorio-estatistico-2023)).

The lender's policy operation sets people using broadband, inferred use, at 146,000 in December 2025 rising to a target of 172,000 by December 2028, with the female figure at 74,000 rising to 87,000 ([operation](2026-03-11-world-bank-sao-tome-dpf-fiscal-energy-digital-connectivity)).

The two are not the same measure - subscriptions against inferred users - and no source reconciles them. What the window adds is a target the state has signed up to, which the regulator's series does not carry.

progress: No change, a first schedule with no earlier tariff held
summary: The incumbent's [published mobile tariffs](2026-01-01-sao-tome-cst-tarifarios-movel) run from 10 dobras for 24 hours to 330 dobras for 30 days, the largest bundle carrying 4,000 MB.
developments:
The schedule lists four bundle families at 24-hour, 7-day and 30-day durations, the entry tier carrying no data allowance and the top tier 4,000 MB for 330 dobras ([tariffs](2026-01-01-sao-tome-cst-tarifarios-movel)).

No earlier schedule is held, so no direction can be stated. Nothing on file gives a price basket, an income comparison or a second operator's tariffs, so affordability in the sense the indicator asks about cannot be computed from what the base holds - only the prices themselves. The page is undated and the year is inferred from the capture.

summary: The [cable to the second island](2025-10-20-world-bank-isr-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-seq7) cut its project rating to moderately satisfactory in October 2025 on procurement difficulties, against installed international [capacity of 35,840 Gb](2024-11-01-sao-tome-ager-observatorio-estatistico-2023) in 2023.
developments:
The lender's status report records that progress towards the development objective declined from satisfactory to moderately satisfactory owing to ongoing challenges with procurement of the cable, while most other project activities progressed and the telecom legal and regulatory framework advanced considerably ([status report](2025-10-20-world-bank-isr-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-seq7)).

The regulator reports installed international broadband capacity of 35,840 Gb in 2023 against 6,122 Gb used ([statistics](2024-11-01-sao-tome-ager-observatorio-estatistico-2023)), so the constraint is not headline capacity on the main island.

Connecting the smaller island remains the single most consequential connectivity item for this country, and a year on the base can say only that its procurement is what slipped.

summary: There is [no active internet exchange point](2026-01-01-sao-tome-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker) and none listed in the peering directory, with an internet resilience score of 30 out of 100.
developments:
The tracker states that no exchange points are active in the country and none are listed in the peering database, and gives a resilience score of 30 out of 100 with 50 per cent of the 1,000 most-visited sites reachable from an in-country server or cache ([tracker](2026-01-01-sao-tome-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker)).

For a two-island state whose only international capacity arrives on one submarine cable ([cable](2015-06-17-world-bank-icr-central-african-backbone-apl2-sao-tome)), the absence of an exchange means domestic traffic between the two networks leaves the country and comes back. The page is a live tracker with no publication date and the year is inferred from the read.

summary: [Satellite internet service was activated](2025-12-11-starlink-begins-service-stp) in December 2025, about ten months after the operator stated an intention to invest.
developments:
Intention to invest was reported in February 2025 and service began in December ([service](2025-12-11-starlink-begins-service-stp), [intention](2025-02-24-starlink-pretende-investir-stp-eua)).

No licence terms, subscriber count, tariff or regulatory condition is published. In an island state whose only submarine cable to its second island is still in build, satellite is the redundancy that arrived first.

summary: The procurement agency [tendered servers and disaster recovery](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital) for the digital identity data centre, and the decision is not confirmed.
developments:
The tender covers servers and a disaster recovery arrangement for the identity data centre, inside a wider government data-centre modernisation ([tender](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

The tender's own body is an attached document that has not been read, so scope, value and specification are unstated. No award or decision is confirmed.

That a disaster recovery arrangement is being procured alongside the primary is worth noting: it is the only redundancy design named anywhere in this ledger.

summary: The state runs a [government data centre and government network dating from 2008](2020-06-01-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-nacional-governacao-digital), with a fibre backbone begun in 2017, and the identity institute [offers hosting to the whole public administration](2026-01-01-inic-sao-tome-alojamento-web-soberania-territorio-nacional).
developments:
The 2020 digital governance strategy is the primary statement of the state's own estate: the data centre and government network from 2008 and the government fibre backbone begun in 2017 ([strategy](2020-06-01-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-nacional-governacao-digital)).

The draft cybersecurity strategy records that both were built with international cooperation and names dependence on external hosting of data and structuring services, including citizens' personal information and critical infrastructure, as an aggravating factor ([cybersecurity strategy](2024-07-23-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-d3)).

The identity institute offers national hosting to the public administration and invites private bodies to use it ([hosting](2026-01-01-inic-sao-tome-alojamento-web-soberania-territorio-nacional)). No capacity figure, tier rating, uptime record or customer count is published for any of it.

summary: The draft cybersecurity strategy [describes no backup or disaster-recovery capability](2024-07-23-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-d3); a [disaster recovery arrangement](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital) was tendered alongside the identity data centre in May 2026.
developments:
The strategy sets objectives on the resilience of critical infrastructures and on incident response plans and a national response team, and describes no backup or disaster-recovery capability anywhere in the state estate ([strategy](2024-07-23-inic-sao-tome-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-d3)).

The procurement agency tendered servers and a disaster recovery arrangement for the identity data centre in May 2026 ([tender](2026-05-14-afap-tender-data-center-servidores-identidade-digital)). The tender's own body is an attached document that has not been read, so scope, value and specification are unstated, and no award is confirmed.

It is the only redundancy design named anywhere in this ledger, and it covers one system rather than the estate the strategy describes as dependent on external hosting.

progress: Mixed, generation and available capacity both fell through 2024 while a four-year rehabilitation project was approved in April 2026
summary: Available generating capacity fell to [33.0 MW at the end of 2024](2025-01-01-sao-tome-emae-principais-indicadores-desempenho-2024) and output by 41 per cent; an [energy transition project](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant) approved in April 2026 will modernise the dispatch centre and rehabilitate networks.
developments:
The utility's own performance report gives available capacity in the plants at 33.0 MW at 31 December 2024 against 39.0 MW in each of the two prior years, maximum capacity referred to production at 15.50 MW against 19.00 MW, and electricity production at 60,764 MWh against 103,533 MWh in 2023 ([report](2025-01-01-sao-tome-emae-principais-indicadores-desempenho-2024)).

The approved project will build a 4 MWp solar plant with a 2 MWh battery on the second island, rehabilitate low-voltage networks, modernise the national dispatch centre and install over 40,000 prepaid meters, against a stated position of daily outages of three to four hours and losses above 34 per cent of generation ([project](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant)).

The gap between installed and usable capacity is what a data centre would sit behind, and it widened over the two years the base can measure.

summary: Generation [fell 41 per cent through 2024](2025-01-01-sao-tome-emae-principais-indicadores-desempenho-2024) with combined efficiency at 58.5 per cent, and [daily outages run three to four hours](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant) with losses above 34 per cent of what is generated.
developments:
The utility reports technical efficiency of 80.0 per cent, commercial efficiency of 73.1 per cent and combined efficiency of 58.5 per cent, on production of 60,764 MWh against 103,533 MWh the year before ([report](2025-01-01-sao-tome-emae-principais-indicadores-desempenho-2024)).

The Court of Auditors' audit of the state's thermal-power investment contract finds the five installed generators do not hold the 10 MW the contract defines and have produced roughly 4 MW since installation, while the state pays for 10 MW; that an investment claim of about 10.85 million euros is unsubstantiated; and that customs and tax exemptions to the company and its group cost the state at least 2.13 million euros, against 13,320,198 litres of fuel the utility supplied free of charge over 2024 ([audit](2025-05-13-sao-tome-tribunal-contas-auditoria-tesla-stp)).

The lender's release states that nearly 95 per cent of generation relies on imported fossil fuels at 0.30 dollars per kilowatt-hour, that daily outages last three to four hours and disrupt hospitals, schools and businesses, and that technical and commercial losses consume more than 34 per cent of electricity generated ([release](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant)).

A [management information system for the utility](2026-08-07-afap-prorroga-solicitacao-novo-sistema-de-informacao-de-gestao-mis-para-a-emae) remains at tender, its deadline extended in August 2026. No state response to the audit, recovery or contract amendment is on the record.

summary: The [national energy compact](2025-01-01-sao-tome-national-energy-compact-mission-300) targets 100 per cent access by 2030 from 84 per cent, and an [approved project](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant) funds island solar, network rehabilitation and 2,000 new connections.
developments:
The compact gives the electricity access rate as 84 per cent in 2024 against a 2030 objective of 100 per cent, with a renewable share of 3 per cent and private capital mobilisation of zero against a target of US$190 million ([compact](2025-01-01-sao-tome-national-energy-compact-mission-300)).

It records that access remains unequal especially in rural areas and that grid extension is expected to cost more owing to very low rural population density, so mini-grids and off-grid alternatives are preferred there ([compact](2025-01-01-sao-tome-national-energy-compact-mission-300)).

The project approved in April 2026 puts a solar plant and battery on the second island, rehabilitates its low-voltage networks and creates 2,000 new connections ([project](2026-04-23-afdb-sao-tome-etreep-245-million-grant)). It is the first funded delivery against the compact's target that the base holds.

summary: The state's own systems were appraised in 2022 as a [fragmented approach to digitization with most foundations still nascent](2022-05-24-world-bank-pad4839-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-project), ranking 155th of 193 on the e-government index.
developments:
The appraisal states that the government has taken a fragmented approach to digitization, that most of the foundations for digital government service delivery are still nascent, and that the country ranks 155th of 193 on the 2020 e-government index and 179th of 193 on the 2018 e-participation index ([appraisal](2022-05-24-world-bank-pad4839-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-project)).

The one dated instance in the window of a government system failing for want of support is the cadastral service, shut out of its rented premises in February 2026 after three and a half years of unpaid state rent ([cadastral service](2026-02-23-sao-tome-servicos-geograficos-cadastrais-paralisados)).

No inventory, refresh cycle, uptime figure or asset register for government hardware is published at any date, so the 2022 appraisal remains the only whole-of-estate statement held.

summary: Four agencies were trained on a [new fishing-vessel registry](2026-05-08-sao-tome-telanon-fao-sistema-registo-embarcacoes-formacao) in April 2026, with a user manual left behind so the system continues in use after the training.
developments:
The training moved vessel registration from paper to an Android application feeding a central database, covering registration and updating of data, consultation, export of reports and information-security practice for technicians of the fisheries directorate, the fisheries inspectorate, the coastguard and the port captaincy ([training](2026-05-08-sao-tome-telanon-fao-sistema-registo-embarcacoes-formacao)).

A user manual was left as permanent support so the system continues in use after the training ([training](2026-05-08-sao-tome-telanon-fao-sistema-registo-embarcacoes-formacao)). That is the only instance in this unit of a handover designed for what happens when the implementing partner leaves.

The standing assessment is the 2022 appraisal's: most foundations for digital government service delivery still nascent ([appraisal](2022-05-24-world-bank-pad4839-digital-sao-tome-and-principe-project)), with a sustainability risk over skilled staffing flagged separately on the property registry ([registry](2024-11-20-worldbank-sao-tome-institutional-capacity-isr-sirp-registo-propriedade)).

summary: The [national cybersecurity strategy for 2024 to 2028](2023-12-15-stp-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-texto-integral) was finalised in December 2023 and [went to public consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca) in September 2025, still unapproved.
developments:
The final text, version 2 of 15 December 2023, sets five strategic objectives: coordination through a Cybersecurity Committee and a national incident response centre, CERT-STP; awareness and a security culture; national capability through training and curricula; consolidation of the legal structure, which it records as lacking any specific legislation on protecting children online; and adoption of good practice, including international standards in software and hardware procurement ([strategy](2023-12-15-stp-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca-texto-integral)).

The regulator put the strategy and its action plan to a 30-day public consultation in September 2025 under the digital project ([consultation](2025-09-01-ager-sao-tome-consulta-publica-estrategia-nacional-ciberseguranca)), and a lender mission listed launching the response team's materialisation as an objective ([mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)). The cybercrime statute has been in force since 2017 and requires a permanent police contact point for international cooperation ([statute](2017-10-06-sao-tome-lei-15-2017-lei-sobre-cibercrime)).

So the law is old and operative, the strategy is written and unapproved almost three years on, and the response team is a mission objective. The action plan's own tracking grids are blank templates in the document, and no incident, capability assessment or exercise is published.

summary: [Resolucao 35/2020](2021-08-09-sao-tome-resolucao-35-2020-estrategia-governacao-digital) mandates an interoperability platform as the structuring layer for public services, and [prototypes were reported live](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) in September 2025.
developments:
The resolution approves the digital governance strategy and creates the digital governance committee, naming an interoperability platform as the structuring layer for integrating and coordinating public services and for recognising and validating multiple citizen identities, alongside an authentication platform on single sign-on and a state certification infrastructure ([resolution](2021-08-09-sao-tome-resolucao-35-2020-estrategia-governacao-digital)).

A lender mission reported data-exchange, portal, credential and electronic-signature prototypes live with a system integrator engaged ([mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

The instrument mandates the platform; it does not record it as built, and no source confirms a production exchange. The framework its interfaces would be specified against is a draft from 2021 ([framework](2021-11-01-inic-sao-tome-quadro-nacional-interoperabilidade-qni-v01)).

summary: The registries directorate operates [legi non](2023-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-legi-non-troca-dados-registos) as the machine-to-machine interface to its life-events database, and [biometric enrolment kits](2025-09-01-sao-tome-afap-kits-biometricos-identidade-digital) were tendered in September 2025.
developments:
The directorate states that the interface is the route by which the root identification of all citizens is to be carried out, allowing electronic validation of paper documents and reliable machine-to-machine exchange between accredited public administration systems through protocols agreed in advance ([interface](2023-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-legi-non-troca-dados-registos)).

The page names no system currently consuming it ([interface](2023-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-legi-non-troca-dados-registos)). Enrolment hardware for the national digital identity was tendered under the digital project in September 2025 ([tender](2025-09-01-sao-tome-afap-kits-biometricos-identidade-digital)).

The social protection additional financing identifies linkage with emerging digital infrastructure such as digital identity as a synergy to be pursued, which places it as an intention rather than an operating exchange ([financing](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon)).

summary: The national health information system runs on an open-source platform [launched in December 2019](2020-01-01-sao-tome-ministerio-saude-sistema-informacao-saude-dhis2), and was put out for [independent evaluation](2026-04-29-sao-tome-pnud-avaliacao-sistema-informacao-saude) in April 2026 alongside two other health systems.
developments:
The health ministry's own page records the platform's official launch on 18 December 2019 and a tracker module launch in October 2020, allowing digital forms and indicators, national-level storage, report generation and visualisation ([platform](2020-01-01-sao-tome-ministerio-saude-sistema-informacao-saude-dhis2)). It does not state that the system exchanges data with any other government system.

The health cooperation strategy records that non-communicable disease indicators were added and that use of the platform had to be optimised in the short term to meet the urgent need for reliable health data ([strategy](2023-07-01-oms-sao-tome-estrategia-cooperacao-pais-2023-2027)).

A one-month independent evaluation was commissioned in April 2026 covering the platform, the supply system and a facilities system by name ([evaluation](2026-04-29-sao-tome-pnud-avaliacao-sistema-informacao-saude)). Three named health systems and no stated interface between them or with anything else.

summary: The school management system was still at implementation stage in 2026, with [technical assistance](2026-04-01-sao-tome-afap-consultoria-implementacao-sige) tendered in April and [national supervision dashboards](2026-05-07-sao-tome-unicef-dashboards-supervisao-educativa) tendered in May.
developments:
The sector compact records that the system was introduced and that the education ministry and the lender are developing it to link information between the central level and the districts, describing the education data layer as a medium-priority enabling factor still being built ([compact](2023-06-01-sao-tome-gpe-pacto-parceria-educacao-sige)).

Specialist technical assistance in technological infrastructure, resource management and training for the system's implementation was tendered in April 2026 ([assistance](2026-04-01-sao-tome-afap-consultoria-implementacao-sige)), and a separate tender opened in May 2026 for a higher education institution to develop dashboards for national education supervision ([dashboards](2026-05-07-sao-tome-unicef-dashboards-supervisao-educativa)).

Two procurements for the same layer, from two different funders, in successive months. Nothing held states an interface between the school system and any other government system.

summary: The social protection information system was rebuilt in 2024 on open-source components and is [integrated with the unique social registry](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon), which holds data on 8,740 families.
developments:
The directorate's own page describes the system as a unified database for registration, management of beneficiaries, monitoring of cash transfers and reporting, with the exchange function it claims internal to the directorate and its partners ([system](2025-04-22-sao-tome-dpssf-sistema-kenon-informacao-protecao-social)).

The project paper records adoption in 2024 of a new open-source management information system, states that for the first time in the country's history it is fully owned and operated by the government, and reports it integrated with the unique social registry, which holds socio-demographic characteristics on 8,740 families, about 16 per cent of the population ([project paper](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon)).

The same paper places digital identity linkage as an intended synergy, not an operating one ([project paper](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon)).

summary: A [foundational digital identity on an open-source platform](2025-06-05 São Tomé and Principe pilots MOSIP-based national digital ID system) has live prototypes for credentials, data exchange, portal and electronic signature, and no source confirms the card itself has launched.
developments:
A system integrator is engaged with the identity institute and the registries directorate, with prototypes live and a roadmap running January to May 2026 ([pilot](2025-06-05 São Tomé and Principe pilots MOSIP-based national digital ID system), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

No source held confirms the foundational card has launched, and the roadmap's delivery is not confirmed either. The identification law that would govern it was flagged as urgent in 2025 and has not passed.

So the components exist as prototypes, the statute does not exist, and whether the thing itself is issued is unestablished.

summary: A [free national identity card campaign](2026-01-22-campanha-bi-gratuito-ilheu-das-rolas) ran in phases including an islet and a diaspora arm, with cards collectable at the embassy in Portugal.
developments:
The campaign ran to an outlying islet in January 2026 and extended to the diaspora, with cards collectable at the embassy in Portugal by June ([campaign](2026-01-22-campanha-bi-gratuito-ilheu-das-rolas), [diaspora](2026-06-25-bi-disponiveis-levantamento-campanha-diaspora-portugal), [embassy](2025-04-07-governo-lanca-sistema-emissao-documentos-embaixada-portugal)).

Free issuance and physical collection at an embassy are the two access designs that matter most in a small island state with a large diaspora, and both are recorded here.

No issuance count, coverage figure or campaign end date is published.

summary: A [passport issuance system](2026-04-15-stp-lanca-sistema-emissao-passaportes-sep-2-0) was launched in April 2026 under a four-year contract with a foreign state mint.
developments:
The system launched under a four-year contract with another country's national printing and minting house ([system](2026-04-15-stp-lanca-sistema-emissao-passaportes-sep-2-0)).

The predecessor system's status is not established in anything held, so what changed is unstated. Passport personalisation held under contract with a foreign state institution is a sovereignty arrangement the record states and does not examine.

summary: [Resolucao 35/2020](2021-08-09-sao-tome-resolucao-35-2020-estrategia-governacao-digital) mandates an authentication platform on single sign-on integrated with digital identity management, and [prototypes are live](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) with no production service confirmed.
developments:
The resolution names a platform based on single sign-on fully integrated with digital identity management and supported by the interoperability platform, alongside a state certification infrastructure providing qualified digital signature ([resolution](2021-08-09-sao-tome-resolucao-35-2020-estrategia-governacao-digital)).

A lender mission reported credential, portal and electronic-signature prototypes live with a system integrator engaged and a roadmap running January to May 2026 ([mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025), [pilot](2025-06-05 São Tomé and Principe pilots MOSIP-based national digital ID system)).

No source confirms an authentication service in production, and the citizen portal that would consume it is in beta ([portal](2026-03-28-inic-lanca-portal-do-cidadao)). Six years on from the mandate, the base holds prototypes.

summary: Birth registration is [entered electronically at every maternity unit](2026-03-10-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-nascimento-electronico-maternidades), free up to one year, with 3,077 births registered in 2025.
developments:
The chief conservator of the civil registry states that free birth registration up to one year is available in every maternity unit in the country, staffed by directorate technicians and trained midwives, and that an electronic system now allows registration to be entered directly into the database from computers and printers at those points, eliminating paper ([registry](2026-03-10-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-nascimento-electronico-maternidades)).

He gives annual birth registrations of 3,077 in 2025, 4,701 in 2021, 3,954 in 2020 and 4,374 in 2019 ([registry](2026-03-10-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-nascimento-electronico-maternidades)), and describes campaigns aimed at mothers who give birth at home and so miss registration at the maternity.

The country diagnostic records the centralised civil registry database as holding birth data from 1920 to 2010 ([diagnostic](2023-01-01-sao-tome-banco-mundial-id4d-diagnostico-sistemas-identificacao)), so the digitised historic series stops fifteen years before the electronic present. Nothing links a birth record to an identity credential issued at birth.

summary: The civil registry is being built out as the technical basis for the electoral register, with [equipment handed over in September 2025](2025-09-09-sao-tome-prese-plataforma-recenseamento-automatico-registo-civil) reinforcing the security of the registry systems.
developments:
The country diagnostic records that the registries directorate began digitising the civil registry and civil identification systems in 2017 and implemented the life-events system in 2018, enabling digital registration of life events across the country ([diagnostic](2023-01-01-sao-tome-banco-mundial-id4d-diagnostico-sistemas-identificacao)).

A public session in September 2025 presented an automatic voter registration platform under development by a Portuguese university, handed over equipment reinforcing the technological component and the security of the civil registry systems, and awarded training certificates to registry and electoral commission technicians ([session](2025-09-09-sao-tome-prese-plataforma-recenseamento-automatico-registo-civil)).

The source does not itself name the life-events system or the identity card as the platform's data sources, and no such linkage is asserted here beyond what it states. The registry is being hardened for one consuming system; the identity credential is a separate build ([mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

summary: The migration service now [issues passports non-presentially](2026-03-23-sao-tome-mne-emissao-passaporte-nao-presencial-diaspora) on a scanned copy of the identity card, whose authenticity it verifies - the first system recorded relying on the national credential.
developments:
The foreign ministry announced that passports are being issued by non-presential means under the amended passport regime, aimed at citizens in the diaspora and particularly where the State has no diplomatic or consular representation, on a signed application form and a copy of a valid identity card whose authenticity is verified by the migration and borders service ([announcement](2026-03-23-sao-tome-mne-emissao-passaporte-nao-presencial-diaspora)).

The verification described is a documentary check on a scanned copy rather than a digital authentication against a register ([announcement](2026-03-23-sao-tome-mne-emissao-passaporte-nao-presencial-diaspora)), which is the distinction the indicator turns on.

The registry's own exchange interface names no consuming system in production ([interface](2023-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-legi-non-troca-dados-registos)), so this is reliance on the credential as a document rather than use of the register as a service.

summary: A [new organic law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp) took effect in June 2025 setting the bank's payment oversight, licensing and consumer-protection mandate, over the [2018 payment system law](2018-09-07-sao-tome-lei-17-2018-sistema-nacional-de-pagamentos) that names it regulator and overseer.
developments:
The organic law replaces the 1992 statute and sets the attributions to regulate and oversee payment systems and to license and supervise financial institutions ([law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp)).

The bank publishes aggregate payment statistics and a payment systems report, last published in August and April 2026 respectively ([statistics](2026-08-28-sao-tome-bcstp-estatisticas-do-sistema-de-pagamentos), [report](2026-04-17-sao-tome-bcstp-relatorio-dos-sistemas-de-pagamentos)), which is the clearest evidence in this unit of a regulator exercising a published oversight function.

It launched a financial technology sandbox in June 2025 under the inclusion strategy ([sandbox](2025-06-03-bcstp-lanca-sandbox-fintechs-inclusao-financeira)); no cohort, admission or graduation has been recorded since.

summary: Vulnerable-family transfers are [executed by bank transfer through the social protection system's payments module](2025-12-12-sao-tome-dpssf-programa-familia-pagamentos-ke-non) with a commercial bank, with [US$6 million in additional financing](2025-10-14-sao-tome-world-bank-social-protection-additional-financing) signed in October 2025.
developments:
The directorate states that the vulnerable families programme transfers are executed by bank transfer using the payments module of the social protection system, in partnership with a commercial bank, and reports the amount disbursed and the households reached across the districts and the Autonomous Region in 2025 ([directorate](2025-12-12-sao-tome-dpssf-programa-familia-pagamentos-ke-non)).

The lender and the government signed an agreement for US$6 million in additional financing to the social protection project, the vehicle through which the transfers are delivered ([agreement](2025-10-14-sao-tome-world-bank-social-protection-additional-financing)).

The project paper describes a new electronic cash transfer payment system through a partnership with a financial institution ([project paper](2025-09-12-sao-tome-banco-mundial-protecao-social-financiamento-adicional-kenon)). Government-to-person is the one payment flow in this unit with a named system, a named bank and a stated coverage.

summary: VAT ran through computer systems from the [2019 code](2019-11-06-sao-tome-lei-13-2019-codigo-do-iva), and by September 2024 [3,866 taxpayers were registered on the VAT system](2025-12-24-sao-tome-world-bank-icr-institutional-capacity-building-project) with collections at 3.32 per cent of GDP.
developments:
The VAT code's preamble states that the tax operates exclusively through computer systems for both declaration and payment, which draws the economic operator into the electronic invoicing system ([code](2019-11-06-sao-tome-lei-13-2019-codigo-do-iva)).

The completion report states that VAT implementation collected the equivalent of 3.32 per cent of GDP in September 2024 with 3,866 taxpayers registered on the system, and that after installation of the central bank core banking system 22 per cent of Treasury and central bank processes were digitalized as of October 2025, with commercial bank interfaces at 20 per cent and cheque compensation at 23 per cent ([report](2025-12-24-sao-tome-world-bank-icr-institutional-capacity-building-project)).

Those are the only digitalisation percentages the base holds for any part of the state, and none is above a quarter.

summary: The [2026 budget law](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado) bars cash payments of 10,000 dobras or more between taxpayers with organised accounting, and a [tax and tourism memorandum](2026-02-10-sao-tome-direccao-dos-impostos-memorando-turismo-e-factura) reinforces the electronic invoicing obligation.
developments:
Article 9 requires such transactions to use a means that identifies the payee - bank transfer, point-of-sale and ATM terminals, nominative cheque or direct debit - and makes cash spending above the limit non-deductible ([budget law](2026-03-23-sao-tome-lei-3-2026-orcamento-geral-do-estado)).

The tax directorate signed a memorandum with the tourism directorate in February 2026 creating a permanent mechanism for sharing data on licensed tourism and hospitality businesses, cross-checking registration and tax compliance and reinforcing the obligation to issue electronic invoices ([memorandum](2026-02-10-sao-tome-direccao-dos-impostos-memorando-turismo-e-factura)).

The enabling statute is the 2018 payment system law, which covers transfers between individuals, commercial entities and financial institutions ([law](2018-09-07-sao-tome-lei-17-2018-sistema-nacional-de-pagamentos)). The window's movement is compulsion rather than capability.

summary: The instrument set is [debit cards, cheques and bank transfers](2026-01-01-sao-tome-bcstp-instrumentos-de-pagamentos), cards on a single domestic network, with the central bank's [payment statistics](2026-08-28-sao-tome-bcstp-estatisticas-do-sistema-de-pagamentos) refreshed to August 2026.
developments:
The central bank's own statement of instruments in use lists debit cards, cheques and bank transfers, with card use regulated by a 2012 notice on the issue and use of bank cards on the domestic network, and transfers described as intrabank, interbank and cross-border ([instruments](2026-01-01-sao-tome-bcstp-instrumentos-de-pagamentos)).

The bank collects, compiles and publishes aggregate statistics on payment operations sent and received by providers, recording the internet banking series from 2014 and the interbank clearing series from 2013 as last published on 28 August 2026, and the card operations series from 2011 as last published on 3 July 2026 ([statistics](2026-08-28-sao-tome-bcstp-estatisticas-do-sistema-de-pagamentos)).

A payment systems report describing developments in the national system was last published on 17 April 2026 ([report](2026-04-17-sao-tome-bcstp-relatorio-dos-sistemas-de-pagamentos)). The series are current; no mobile money or wallet instrument appears in any of them.

summary: The financial inclusion index [rose to 0.41 in 2025 from 0.24 in 2017](2025-11-01-bcstp-segundo-inquerito-inclusao-literacia-financeiras-texto-integral), still 'moderate' on the AFI scale, while bank-account holding stagnated at minus 0.6 points.
developments:
The 2021 to 2025 inclusion strategy reports the 2017 demand-side survey finding that 76 per cent of the population over 18 was excluded from the financial system, that 39 per cent of respondents and 15 per cent of women held a bank account, and that the inclusion index was around 0.24, and 0.18 for women ([strategy](2021-01-01-sao-tome-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-2021-2025)).

The central bank's second demand-side survey puts the index at 0.41 in 2025, the women's index at 0.34, the gender banking gap at 4.8 percentage points from 20, and bank-account holding down 0.6 points, which it attributes to the low income of the 30 per cent of adults at the bottom ([survey](2025-11-01-bcstp-segundo-inquerito-inclusao-literacia-financeiras-texto-integral)). Its financial literacy barometer averages 72 per cent across seven dimensions against 39 in 2017, a rise it says is partly a refinement of method ([barometer](2025-11-01-bcstp-segundo-inquerito-inclusao-literacia-financeiras-texto-integral)).

The report does not restate the headline adult exclusion rate, so the [2017 exclusion figure](2021-01-01-sao-tome-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-2021-2025) has no direct 2025 counterpart in what the base holds.

summary: The [1999 exchange law](1999-10-26-sao-tome-lei-cambial-decreto-lei-32-99) makes the central bank the exchange authority and routes current transfers through the commercial banks; [repatriation and surrender requirements](2025-12-05-sao-tome-imf-country-report-25-347-second-review-ecf) were under review in December 2025.
developments:
The law subjects exchange operations to central bank regulation and provides for sales of foreign currency and transfers abroad relating to imports and current invisibles to be carried out by the commercial banks ([law](1999-10-26-sao-tome-lei-cambial-decreto-lei-32-99)).

The second review under the credit facility reports on the effect of the foreign-exchange repatriation and surrender requirements on the central bank's reserve position ([review](2025-12-05-sao-tome-imf-country-report-25-347-second-review-ecf)).

The central bank describes transfers as intrabank, interbank and cross-border ([instruments](2026-01-01-sao-tome-bcstp-instrumentos-de-pagamentos)). No remittance corridor volume, cost or provider is published, which for a state with a large diaspora is the gap that matters most here.

summary: A [new central bank organic law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp) replaced the 1992 statute in June 2025, carrying the duty relied on for financial consumer protection and for inclusion and literacy.
developments:
The law sets out the bank's attributions including regulating and overseeing payment systems, licensing and supervising financial institutions, and the duty relied on for financial consumer protection and financial inclusion and literacy ([law](2025-06-05-sao-tome-lei-3-2025-lei-organica-do-bcstp)). The capture is truncated at the fetch limit, so the later articles are not readable here.

No complaints procedure, ombudsman, disclosure rule or published redress statistic sits behind the duty in anything the base holds, and the sandbox launched in 2025 has no published cohort ([sandbox](2025-06-03-bcstp-lanca-sandbox-fintechs-inclusao-financeira)).

A mandate stated in an organic law is where consumer protection starts, not where it is delivered.

summary: A [central civil and criminal identification service](2026-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-centro-de-identificacao-civil-e-criminal) keeps the national records, and a [free identity-card campaign closed in March 2026](2026-03-19-sao-tome-campanha-nacional-bilhete-de-identidade-gratuito) feeding automatic voter registration.
developments:
The registries directorate describes the centre as the central service charged with centralising, organising and keeping up to date at national level the records on civil and criminal identification, seated in the capital with jurisdiction over the whole territory ([service](2026-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-centro-de-identificacao-civil-e-criminal)).

A national campaign giving a free identity card to every citizen over 17 without a valid one ran until 15 March 2026, implemented by the directorate with technical and financial support from the electoral reform project, and the card is to become the base document for automatic and permanent voter registration ([campaign](2026-03-19-sao-tome-campanha-nacional-bilhete-de-identidade-gratuito)).

No population coverage figure, issuance total or de-duplication statement is published for the register itself. The page describing the service carries no date and the year is inferred.

summary: The life-events system has run nationally since 2018, and birth registration is now [entered electronically at every maternity unit](2026-03-10-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-nascimento-electronico-maternidades), eliminating paper at the point of birth.
developments:
The directorate's service page sets out the registrable acts - birth registration including free registration under one year, acknowledgement of paternity, marriage and transcription, name changes, nationality and death entries - with fees, deadlines and the offices at which each is requested ([services](2026-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-civil-servicos)).

The country diagnostic records the system as implemented in 2018 enabling digital registration of life events across the country, with a centralised database holding birth data from 1920 to 2010 ([diagnostic](2023-01-01-sao-tome-banco-mundial-id4d-diagnostico-sistemas-identificacao)).

The chief conservator reports registration entered directly into the database from computers at every maternity, with 3,077 births and 1,063 deaths registered in 2025 ([registry](2026-03-10-sao-tome-dgrn-registo-nascimento-electronico-maternidades)). Death registration is a quarter of birth registration and nothing held explains the gap.

summary: There is no enacted national address register; the [postal base bill](2022-08-01-sao-tome-proposta-de-lei-40-xi-lei-de-base-postal) referring to a postcode system and an address database was submitted for debate and is not shown in force.
developments:
The parliamentary gazette carries the government's postal base bill, which refers to a postal code system and an address database among the postal service obligations ([bill](2022-08-01-sao-tome-proposta-de-lei-40-xi-lei-de-base-postal)).

It is a bill submitted for debate, not an enacted law, and the record consulted does not show it in force ([bill](2022-08-01-sao-tome-proposta-de-lei-40-xi-lei-de-base-postal)). Four years on, nothing records its passage.

The absence bears on more than post: the property registry holds an estimated 162,000 property records ([registry](2024-11-20-worldbank-sao-tome-institutional-capacity-isr-sirp-registo-propriedade)) with no national addressing scheme behind them.

summary: The [company one-stop window](2026-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-guiche-unico-para-empresa) performs formation, alteration, dissolution and branch filings and requires the taxpayer identifier throughout, over a [modernisation diagnostic](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025) completed in 2025.
developments:
The directorate's page sets out the acts performed - company formation, alteration of the articles, dissolution, branch registration and sole-trader registration - and shows the taxpayer identifier in operational use: the taxpayer card is required of the applicant, the identifier of shareholders, foreign non-resident partners and companies, and a negative certificate of tax debt is required to dissolve ([window](2026-01-01-sao-tome-dgrn-guiche-unico-para-empresa)).

A legal and technical diagnostic toward a modern, data-oriented registry was presented by a lender mission in September 2025, with the directorate and the identity institute flagging the need for offline access given electricity and internet limits ([diagnostic](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

The window is operating and the modernisation is a diagnostic. No registration count, turnaround figure or online filing route is published.

summary: The social protection directorate [stated a coverage figure for the single social registry](2026-08-03-direcao-da-protecao-social-esclarece-sobre-cadastro-social-unico-stp) and clarified that it is not a poverty count.
developments:
The single social register now covers more than 12,500 households, up from 8,000, and the vulnerable families programme is to expand from 5,000 to 6,000 households, on the prime minister's account ([statement](2026-08-26-sao-tome-csu-social-registry-expansion)).

The clarification was issued in August 2026 ([clarification](2026-08-03-direcao-da-protecao-social-esclarece-sobre-cadastro-social-unico-stp), [mission](2025-09-17-world-bank-ajuda-memoria-stp-digital-setembro-2025)).

An agency publicly correcting a misreading of its own registry figure is unusual in this frame and worth recording as such: a registry count measures who is enrolled, not who is poor, and conflating the two misstates both.
